# Scientific review: weighted complete-split edge norms

**Correctness (C): PASS.** The claim concerns the real free 2-convex lattice generated by a finite Euclidean space, with edges represented by unnormalized incidence vectors and edge amplitudes multiplying those vectors. Its norm is the Hilbert-to-maximum-coordinate absolutely two-summing norm. Finite-dimensional Pietsch domination and convex minimax reduce the unrestricted norm to the maximum trace square root of the probability-weighted incidence Gramian. Coordinate-permutation averaging is valid by matrix-trace concavity, and the three orthogonal Laplacian eigenvalues in the proof establish the precise one-variable formula. Strict concavity, the derivative at zero, and Cauchy–Schwarz prove both branches and the sharp crossing; global supporting-hyperplane inequalities independently establish the necessary-and-sufficient heterogeneous-edge screening rule. The asymptotic and second-derivative formulas follow from explicit algebra. The accompanying checker passed 58 configurations, including eight optimizations over all edge probabilities and six heterogeneous designs. Its finite experiments are supplementary, not proofs of the infinite parameter theorem. The theorem does not classify every nonsymmetric optimal design.

**Originality (O): PASS, with documented residual risk.** The closest mathematical antecedents are the general free-convex-lattice norm formula in Jardón-Sánchez et al. (arXiv:2101.03510, full accessible article Sections 1, 6 and 7 inspected), the previously established complete-bipartite norm (the exact baseline in this theorem), and distinct three-part graph two-summing screening results. The closest same-graph result concerns the John ellipsoid of a Lipschitz-dual polytope; optimization of determinant under slab containment does not imply this new trace-square-root two-summing norm or its continuously weighted clique phase diagram. Das–Liu's accessible abstract addresses recognition of split graphs by Laplacian spectra rather than the optimized two-summing invariant. Searches also examined edge-operator terminology and optimal design equivalences. A less-indexed equivalent theorem cannot be entirely ruled out; unavailable full text is recorded as residual risk, not represented as read.

**Mathematical value (V): PASS.** The precise object is a natural graph-generated norm in free convex Banach-lattice theory, rather than an arbitrary statistic. The complete split graph continuously deforms the complete bipartite base by adding all edges within one part. The sharp full-parameter norm formula and its iff heterogeneous screening law reveal that many arbitrarily large pointwise changes can have zero effect on this non-Hilbertian operator-ideal norm. The dimension-imbalance fourth-root law makes the largest screened amplitude unbounded, while an exact curvature jump describes the onset of norm growth. These quantitative phenomena are not consequences of graph-Laplacian eigenvalues alone without solving the nontrivial weight optimization.

**Closest sources and remaining limitations.** Jardón-Sánchez et al., *Free Banach lattices under convexity conditions*, arXiv:2101.03510, DOI 10.1007/s13398-021-01155-8; K. C. Das and M. Liu, *Complete split graph determined by its (signless) Laplacian spectrum*, DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2016.01.003 (abstract inspected, article body not available); A. Pietsch, *Operator Ideals* (standard background). The result is restricted to real exponent two and Euclidean generators. The scientific novelty review is qualified by incomplete coverage of nonindexed operator-ideal literature.

Self-review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
